pr.title: fix(langgraph): detect subgraphs from bytecode instead of source
pr.body:
Fixes langchain-ai/langgraph#8559

`find_subgraph_pregel` runs once per node at build time and recovers each node function's reachable values with `inspect.getsource` + `ast.parse`; langchain-ai/langgraph#8559 measures that source parsing at 80% of `StateGraph.compile()`. This replaces it with a `dis` walk over `func.__code__`, which reads the same information already in memory.

Closure cells and the globals named in `co_names` supply the values directly, and a walk over the instruction stream recovers the attribute paths the function actually takes. The closure alone cannot express those: a captured `holder` whose graph lives at `holder.graph` is reachable only if something records that `graph` is loaded off `holder`.

Both implementations over-declare — a node can reference a graph it never invokes — and this one over-declares a different set. It no longer reports a graph named only along an attribute path in code the compiler removed; such a path cannot execute, so that entry was always a phantom. Nothing that can actually run stopped being detected. `find_subgraph_pregel` returns the first `PregelProtocol` it finds, so the remaining extra candidates only widen detection.

## Release note

Subgraph auto-detection now reads node functions' bytecode instead of parsing their source. Graph builds with many function-backed nodes are substantially faster, and subgraphs are now detected inside functions with no retrievable source — defined in a REPL or notebook cell, or via `exec` — where detection previously failed silently and returned nothing.

## Performance

Against [langgraph-build-bench](<https://github.com/soarez/langgraph-build-bench>) — 713 nodes, 500 state fields, 264 tools; CPython 3.12.8, Apple silicon:

```
before   build 1412 ms   subgraph detection 1132 ms  (80%)
after    build  286 ms   subgraph detection    4 ms   (2%)
```

**4.9x on total build, \~266x on detection.** The bench prints whole ms; at full precision detection is 1139 ms -> 4.23 ms.

review_comments.body:
This holds when the captured value *is* the graph, but not when the graph sits one attribute off it. The closure root survives; the `LOAD_ATTR` chain doesn't, and `co_names` keeps the names without their order or depth, so there's nothing left to reconstruct from.

```python
holder = Box(child_graph)

def node(state):
    if False:
        holder.payload.invoke(state)   # the only place `.payload` appears
    return {"log": []}
```

Reverting only this file to `origin/main` and rerunning the same shapes: main resolves it, this branch returns `None`. Same for code after `return`, for `while False:`, and at any chain depth. Checked on 3.10, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14. A dead-code *root* (`if False: sub.invoke()`, where `sub` is the graph) does still resolve, so this is narrower than it sounds.

To be clear about how much this matters: I ran both implementations end to end through `find_subgraph_pregel` over every live function object after importing `langgraph`, `prebuilt`, `langchain_core` and the test suite, 19,981 to 31,093 functions per version across 3.10-3.14, and got **zero** detection differences. So nothing real is hitting this.

Given that, I don't think it's worth chasing in code. Recovering the path means guessing name sequences, which is exponential in depth, and a source-parse fallback would fire on 54% of the functions I swept, which is exactly the cost this PR removes. But could we drop "superset" from the description and name the limit instead? Something like: *an attribute path that appears only in code the compiler removes is not recoverable from bytecode; a captured value that is itself a graph still resolves, which is the common form.* Better a documented boundary than one someone finds later.

+"""Tests for subgraph auto-detection (`pregel/_utils.py`).
+
+Detection failing is silent — the graph still runs, only introspection goes
+quiet — so every shape a node can hold a graph in is pinned here. The expected
+values are what the source-parsing implementation this replaced produced for
+the same shapes, except for `sourceless`, whose source it could not read, and
+`empty_closure_cell`, on which it raised.
+"""
+
+import functools
+import operator
+from typing import Annotated, Any
+
+import pytest
+from typing_extensions import TypedDict
+
+from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
+from langgraph.pregel._utils import get_function_nonlocals
+
+
+class State(TypedDict):
+    log: Annotated[list, operator.add]
+
+
+def _leaf(tag: str) -> Any:
+    """Return a compiled graph that reports itself as `tag`."""
+    builder = StateGraph(State)
+    builder.add_node(tag, lambda s: {"log": [tag]})
+    builder.add_edge(START, tag)
+    builder.add_edge(tag, END)
+    compiled = builder.compile()
+    compiled.name = tag
+    return compiled
+
+
+def _detect(node: Any) -> str | None:
+    """Return the name of the subgraph detected for `node`, or None."""
+    builder = StateGraph(State)
+    builder.add_node("n", node)
+    builder.add_edge(START, "n")
+    builder.add_edge("n", END)
+    subgraphs = builder.compile().nodes["n"].subgraphs
+    return getattr(subgraphs[0], "name", "?") if subgraphs else None
+
+
+class _Box:
+    def __init__(self, payload: Any) -> None:
+        self.payload = payload
+
+
+class _ListSubclass(list):
+    pass
+
+
+class _MethodHolder:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.graph = _leaf("via_self")
+
+    def as_node(self, state: State) -> Any:
+        return self.graph.invoke(state)
+
+
+MODULE_GRAPH = _leaf("module_global")
+CHAIN = _Box(_Box(_leaf("attr_chain")))
+GRAPH_IN_PLAIN_LIST = [_leaf("in_list")]
+METHOD_HOLDER = _MethodHolder()
+
+
+def closure_capture() -> Any:
+    sub = _leaf("closure")
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return sub.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def module_global() -> Any:
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return MODULE_GRAPH.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def attribute_chain() -> Any:
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return CHAIN.payload.payload.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def nested_def_captured_attribute() -> Any:
+    """A chain on a captured holder, named only inside a nested code object.
+
+    The captured value is the holder, not the graph, so the chain itself has to
+    be recovered from the nested scope.
+    """
+    holder = _Box(_leaf("nested_captured"))
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        def inner() -> Any:
+            return holder.payload.invoke(state)
+
+        return inner()
+
+    return node
+
+

review_comments.body:
The docstring didn't move with the body. It says "the nonlocal variables accessed by a function", but what comes back now is captured cell values whether or not the bytecode names them, plus globals from `co_names`, plus every intermediate along an attribute path. `Returns: List[Any]:` also restates the annotation, in the old capital-`List` spelling.

The wording predates this PR so it's fair to leave it, but the body underneath is entirely new, so it seemed worth raising while we're here.

+    return compiled

+
+def _detect(node: Any) -> str | None:
+    """Return the name of the subgraph detected for `node`, or None."""
+    builder = StateGraph(State)

+    builder.add_edge(START, "n")
+    builder.add_edge("n", END)

+
+
+class _Box:
+    def __init__(self, payload: Any) -> None:
+        self.payload = payload
+
+
+class _ListSubclass(list):
+    pass
+
+
+class _MethodHolder:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.graph = _leaf("via_self")
+
+    def as_node(self, state: State) -> Any:
+        return self.graph.invoke(state)
+
+
+MODULE_GRAPH = _leaf("module_global")
+CHAIN = _Box(_Box(_leaf("attr_chain")))
+GRAPH_IN_PLAIN_LIST = [_leaf("in_list")]
+METHOD_HOLDER = _MethodHolder()
+
+
+def closure_capture() -> Any:
+    sub = _leaf("closure")
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return sub.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def module_global() -> Any:
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return MODULE_GRAPH.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def attribute_chain() -> Any:
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return CHAIN.payload.payload.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def nested_def_captured_attribute() -> Any:
+    """A chain on a captured holder, named only inside a nested code object.
+
+    The captured value is the holder, not the graph, so the chain itself has to
+    be recovered from the nested scope.
+    """

+
+def unreachable_branch() -> Any:
+    """A captured graph referenced only from code the compiler removes."""
+    sub = _leaf("unreachable")

+    return node

+
+def wrapper_referencing_nothing() -> Any:
+    """A wrapper whose own scope holds nothing, so only `__wrapped__` leads on.
+
+    `functools.wraps` would leave the wrapper closing over the inner function;

+    sub = _leaf("via_wrapped")
+
+    def inner(state: State) -> Any:
+        return sub.invoke(state)
+
+    def wrapper(state: State) -> Any:

+
+
+def captured_list_subclass() -> Any:
+    """A `list` subclass is not a leaf: it can carry a graph as an attribute."""
+    holder = _ListSubclass()
+    holder.payload = _leaf("list_subclass")
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return holder.payload.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def empty_closure_cell() -> Any:
+    """An unassigned closure variable leaves a cell that cannot be read."""
+    sub = _leaf("beside_empty_cell")
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return unassigned, sub.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+    unassigned = 1  # never runs, so the cell it creates is never filled
+
+
+def sourceless() -> Any:
+    """A node compiled without a source file, which `getsource` could not read."""
+    namespace: dict[str, Any] = {"SOURCELESS": _leaf("sourceless")}

+        compile(
+            "def node(state):\n    return SOURCELESS.invoke(state)", "<test>", "exec"
+        ),
+        namespace,
+    )
+    return namespace["node"]
+
+
+async def _async_node(state: State) -> Any:
+    return await MODULE_GRAPH.ainvoke(state)
+
+
+def async_node() -> Any:
+    return _async_node
+
+
+def no_subgraph() -> Any:
+    """Nothing but leaf values in reach, so the bytecode walk is skipped."""
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return {"log": [len("abc") + 1]}
+
+    return node
+
+
+def recombined_names() -> Any:
+    """Loads `CHAIN.payload` and `local.payload`, never `CHAIN.payload.payload`."""
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        local = _Box("not a graph")
+        return {"log": [CHAIN.payload, local.payload]}
+
+    return node
+
+
+def broken_attribute_chain() -> Any:
+    holder = _Box("a string, so `.payload.missing` cannot resolve")
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return holder.payload.missing.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def nested_def_global() -> Any:
+    """A global named only in a nested code object: out of reach, as before."""
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        def inner() -> Any:
+            return MODULE_GRAPH.invoke(state)
+
+        return inner()
+
+    return node
+
+
+def graph_in_plain_list() -> Any:
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return GRAPH_IN_PLAIN_LIST[0].invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def bound_method_self() -> Any:
+    return METHOD_HOLDER.as_node
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("factory", "expected"),
+    [
+        (closure_capture, "closure"),
+        (module_global, "module_global"),
+        (attribute_chain, "attr_chain"),
+        (nested_def_captured_attribute, "nested_captured"),
+        (unreachable_branch, "unreachable"),
+        (wrapper_referencing_nothing, "via_wrapped"),
+        (captured_list_subclass, "list_subclass"),
+        (empty_closure_cell, "beside_empty_cell"),
+        (sourceless, "sourceless"),
+        (async_node, "module_global"),
+        # Shapes no reference chain reaches: a subscript, an instance attribute
+        # of `self`, and a global named only in a nested scope.
+        (no_subgraph, None),
+        (recombined_names, None),
+        (broken_attribute_chain, None),
+        (nested_def_global, None),
+        (graph_in_plain_list, None),
+        (bound_method_self, None),
+    ],
+    ids=lambda value: value.__name__ if callable(value) else str(value),
+)
+def test_detects_subgraph(factory: Any, expected: str | None) -> None:

review_comments.body: Thanks for running that sweep, that's useful! I agree that "Superset" is strictly incorrect. Reworded. I must point out though that these subgraphs no longer being identified, when they could not be invoked anyway (since the compiler drops the code path) is actually an improvement, i.e. identifying less of these non-invokable subgraphs (false-positives). Added your test case.

+
+def closure_capture() -> Any:

+
+
+def module_global() -> Any:

+
+    return node
+
+
+def attribute_chain() -> Any:
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return CHAIN.payload.payload.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def nested_def_captured_attribute() -> Any:
+    """A chain on a captured holder, named only inside a nested code object.
+
+    The captured value is the holder, not the graph, so the chain itself has to
+    be recovered from the nested scope.
+    """
+    holder = _Box(_leaf("nested_captured"))
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        def inner() -> Any:
+            return holder.payload.invoke(state)
+
+        return inner()
+
+    return node
+
+
+def unreachable_branch() -> Any:
+    """A captured graph referenced only from code the compiler removes."""
+    sub = _leaf("unreachable")
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:

+    return node
+
+
+def wrapper_referencing_nothing() -> Any:
+    """A wrapper whose own scope holds nothing, so only `__wrapped__` leads on.
+

+    setting the attribute by hand does not.

+    sub = _leaf("via_wrapped")
+
+    def inner(state: State) -> Any:
+        return sub.invoke(state)
+
+    def wrapper(state: State) -> Any:
+        return {"log": []}

+    wrapper.__wrapped__ = inner
+    return wrapper
+
+
+def captured_list_subclass() -> Any:

+    holder.payload = _leaf("list_subclass")

+        return holder.payload.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def empty_closure_cell() -> Any:
+    """An unassigned closure variable leaves a cell that cannot be read."""
+    sub = _leaf("beside_empty_cell")
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return unassigned, sub.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+    unassigned = 1  # never runs, so the cell it creates is never filled
+
+
+def sourceless() -> Any:
+    """A node compiled without a source file, which `getsource` could not read."""
+    namespace: dict[str, Any] = {"SOURCELESS": _leaf("sourceless")}
+    exec(

+        ),
+        namespace,
+    )
+    return namespace["node"]
+
+
+async def _async_node(state: State) -> Any:
+    return await MODULE_GRAPH.ainvoke(state)
+
+
+def async_node() -> Any:
+    return _async_node
+
+
+def no_subgraph() -> Any:
+    """Nothing but leaf values in reach, so the bytecode walk is skipped."""
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return {"log": [len("abc") + 1]}
+
+    return node
+
+
+def recombined_names() -> Any:
+    """Loads `CHAIN.payload` and `local.payload`, never `CHAIN.payload.payload`."""
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        local = _Box("not a graph")
+        return {"log": [CHAIN.payload, local.payload]}
+
+    return node
+
+
+def broken_attribute_chain() -> Any:
+    holder = _Box("a string, so `.payload.missing` cannot resolve")
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return holder.payload.missing.invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def nested_def_global() -> Any:
+    """A global named only in a nested code object: out of reach, as before."""
+
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        def inner() -> Any:
+            return MODULE_GRAPH.invoke(state)
+
+        return inner()
+
+    return node
+
+
+def graph_in_plain_list() -> Any:
+    def node(state: State) -> Any:
+        return GRAPH_IN_PLAIN_LIST[0].invoke(state)
+
+    return node
+
+
+def bound_method_self() -> Any:
+    return METHOD_HOLDER.as_node
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("factory", "expected"),
+    [
+        (closure_capture, "closure"),
+        (module_global, "module_global"),
+        (attribute_chain, "attr_chain"),
+        (nested_def_captured_attribute, "nested_captured"),
+        (unreachable_branch, "unreachable"),
+        (wrapper_referencing_nothing, "via_wrapped"),
+        (captured_list_subclass, "list_subclass"),
+        (empty_closure_cell, "beside_empty_cell"),
+        (sourceless, "sourceless"),
+        (async_node, "module_global"),
+        # Shapes no reference chain reaches: a subscript, an instance attribute
+        # of `self`, and a global named only in a nested scope.
+        (no_subgraph, None),
+        (recombined_names, None),
+        (broken_attribute_chain, None),
+        (nested_def_global, None),
+        (graph_in_plain_list, None),
+        (bound_method_self, None),
+    ],
+    ids=lambda value: value.__name__ if callable(value) else str(value),
+)
